entries.title: What's new in 0.5.0
entries.body: v0.5.0 adds entry tags with filter, a first-run onboarding tour with spotlight anchoring, cross-application image drag-and-drop, and IndexNow integration for the marketing website, along with multi-layer network isolation hardening, unlock/lock blur animations, a sticky editor toolbar, per-item toolbar configuration, font family and font size in the editor toolbar, and a centralized plugins directory. Error messages across several dialogs have been sanitized, a multi-auth duplicate-credential vulnerability has been fixed, and the entire codebase has been substantially refactored with expanded test coverage.

entries.title: What's new in 0.4.22
entries.body: Mini Diarium v0.4.22 bundles two new open-source Arabic-capable fonts (Amiri and Tajawal), replaces the folder picker with a direct `.db` file selector for opening existing journals, caps the journal picker list to 5 visible items with scrolling, and optimizes word-count calculation to sub-microsecond performance on both plain text and TipTap HTML paths.

entries.title: What's new in 0.4.21
entries.body: v0.4.21 adds text color and highlight formatting, export date/month filters, auto-focus on unlock, and a French locale. It fixes bundled fonts not loading in macOS/Windows release builds, moves Underline to the basic toolbar, and makes the Preferences dialog responsive.

entries.title: What's new in 0.4.19
entries.body: New setting to require all authentication methods at once, native right-to-left text support in the editor, and a fix for German users seeing English interface text.

entries.title: What's new in 0.4.17
entries.body: Introduced the in-app notification center and applied security hardening fixes.

entries.title: Documentation website is live
entries.body: A full user guide is now available online — covering every feature from writing entries and navigating your journal to import/export, plugins, and security.

entries.title: Mini Diarium is on Flathub
entries.body: Linux users can now install Mini Diarium directly from Flathub. The Flatpak package is sandboxed, uses no network access, and integrates with XDG portals for file dialogs.
